review.verdict: The department reached 10/10 done-when on site v4 at 40/40 spend, but a Requester-answer parsing failure cost a second cycle and about 20 messages ([24]-[44]), and 'done' means a page structure full of marked placeholders.

identity.note: Stayed in role and closed correctly [54], but did not act on Adaptation's budget question [8] until Audit flagged it [21]. Also stated the raise as done [25] when code had not applied it, and mixed A/B and 1/2 labels across [22], [30], [33]. It asked for the digit only at [41], the fourth ask.

adaptation.note: Surfaced the 50 vs 35 gap at once [4], revised honestly [6], parked at exchange 4 [38], and invented nothing. Weak point: its first cut was the pre-order form [4], although pre-order is named in the brief. Declining to propose in [40] was sensible cost discipline.

priority.note: Clear refuse-at-5, grant-at-40 position [37] with measurable stop-loss. But it quoted 35 [5] then corrected to 30 [7], and issued a GRANT of 10 against 5 remaining [27], which code turned into a REFUSE (the one invalid move).

coordination.note: Stated its scheduling rule every turn and used the single-writer lock. It added an Audit dependency [10], then removed it because it was not declared [13]. Nothing needed holding.

audit.note: Correct on item 6 and its routing [21], and the verdicts match the code tally and mechanical checks. Visible evidence is the tally, not file quotes, so how deeply it read the file is unverified.

builder.note: Each build matched its workflow and reported scope [12][15][18][50]. File is 33.5 KB, under the 60 KB limit, with no JS errors. 'Nothing else changed' is self-reported and only partly checkable via Audit.

went_well: Funding gap named in the first Adaptation message [4]; no wrong trade of gallery vs farms, as the charter rule required.
Zero validator refusals, zero held workflows, 4 of 4 workflows done, 2 conflicts settled by agents without Identity.
Mechanical checks (overflow at 360px and 1280px, JS errors, broken links) ran on both versions and were clean [20][52].
Budget raise stayed under Requester control and was recorded only after a clear answer [44].
problems: Three 'A' replies [24][32][35] did not raise the budget. The first failure has no event or system message; the budget only showed as unchanged when Priority's GRANT was refused [28].
Adaptation asked about the 5 gap at [8]. Identity first spoke to the Requester at [22], after build and Audit, so the budget question waited about 14 messages.
Priority funded 30 of 35 and left 5 idle, knowing pre-order needed 10 [7]. That produced a known 9/10 audit in cycle 1.
Identity never asked the Requester for content at J2.a [2]. All four Requester questions were about budget or the answer format. Menu, hours, farms and photos are all placeholders (9 open inputs).
All four workflows charged exactly the estimate (10 each), so the run says nothing about whether agents estimate cost well.
learnings: Test system: accept letter or digit answers, or show one label scheme only; this is the biggest cost driver here ([24] to [44]).
Test system: post a visible 'applied / not applied' line after every Requester answer that should change state. The silent failure at [24] hid the cause.
J2 design: if Adaptation raises a budget gap to Identity, require Identity to ask the Requester before the build starts. Test whether that avoids the cycle-2 rework.
J2 design: Priority should not GRANT contingent on an unrecorded raise [27]; it should COUNTER or hand to Identity. Keep the code budget check.
Test next: a brief with real menu, hours and farm facts, plus a variant where Identity must ask for content up front. As scored, 'done' is cheap with placeholders.
Test system: price workflows differently so estimate vs charge can differ; the flat rate card gives no signal.
Keep: stated scheduling rule, code-run mechanical checks, parking at exchange 4.
